payload.comment: Comparison stage is internally consistent and arithmetically correct. Verified: agentic_accuracy (0.921448) − baseline_accuracy (0.840251) = 0.081197, matching the reported accuracy_delta. Both models share the same seed (47) and split fingerprint (9afc9ed3…c7505), ensuring a fair like-for-like evaluation on identical data. The baseline is a fixed tiny_cnn control (hidden=16, depth=2, 15 epochs) while the agentic run is ResNet18 (hidden=48 base width; depth field inactive per fixed-topology policy). Transformer-specific fields in the baseline config (num_heads, patch_size, pooling, positional_encoding, mlp_ratio, tokenizer_layers) are correctly inactive for the CNN family and do not alter the architecture. The 8.12 pp improvement is meaningful and the baseline is met/exceeded. No deterministic findings are present. The OOD AUROC warning (0.3938 < 0.5, anti-correlated confidence at σ≥0.25) is already tracked at warning severity in the abstention and reporting stages; it does not invalidate the in-distribution accuracy comparison and does not constitute a deterministic finding requiring stop. Class 7 (cancer-associated stroma) recall of 56.5% and the ~7.5 pp val-test gap are noted observations carried forward from evaluation; they do not affect the comparison's validity. Proceed to next stage.
llm_issues: warning: OOD AUROC (0.3938) below random chance is a known limitation of the max_softmax abstention mechanism at σ≥0.25; already tracked in abstention/reporting stages, does not block comparison
info: Class 7 (cancer-associated stroma) recall 56.5% (F1=0.70) is the weakest class; 110/421 misclassified primarily to smooth muscle (63) and debris (47); carried from evaluation stage
info: Val-test accuracy gap ~7.5 pp (99.60% val vs 92.14% test) noted as generalization observation; not a pipeline defect
